headline_marked: 12 ex-advisers [[condemn harassment of Prof Yunus]] at New York airport
headline: 12 ex-advisers condemn harassment of Prof Yunus at New York airport
summary: Former advisers of the interim government express outrage over a video showing protesters shouting at the Nobel laureate at JFK airport.
details: A group of 12 former advisers to the interim government have issued a statement strongly condemning the harassment of Nobel laureate Professor Muhammad Yunus at New York's JFK airport.
A video circulating on social media shows protesters shouting at Professor Yunus as he left the airport in a wheelchair, asking him 'Why you come here?' and making other derogatory remarks.
The harassment is alleged to have been carried out by expatriate supporters of the banned Awami League.
The former advisers described the incident as part of a planned attack and a campaign of misinformation and online harassment targeting the Professor.
They emphasized that the interim government worked tirelessly to rebuild the country after years of economic looting, corruption, and widespread human rights violations.
The statement further noted that the interim government ended heinous acts like enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings that were common under the previous regime.
The advisers asserted that their resolve to fulfill the 'July promises' remains unshaken despite threats, lies, or personal harassment.
They concluded that the historical public support for reforms and dignity, earned through the sacrifices of youth, cannot be erased by the malicious propaganda of the ousted regime's supporters.
caption:
Nobel laureate Professor Muhammad Yunus was shouted at and harassed at JFK airport in New York. 12 former advisers have now spoken out in outrage.

A group of 12 former advisers to the interim government have issued a statement strongly condemning the harassment of Nobel laureate Professor Muhammad Yunus at New York's JFK airport.

A video circulating on social media shows protesters shouting at Professor Yunus as he left the airport in a wheelchair, asking him 'Why you come here?' and making other derogatory remarks.

The harassment is alleged to have been carried out by expatriate supporters of the banned Awami League.

The former advisers described the incident as part of a planned attack and a campaign of misinformation and online harassment targeting the Professor.

They emphasized that the interim government worked tirelessly to rebuild the country after years of economic looting, corruption, and widespread human rights violations.

The statement further noted that the interim government ended heinous acts like enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings that were common under the previous regime.

The advisers asserted that their resolve to fulfill the 'July promises' remains unshaken despite threats, lies, or personal harassment.

They concluded that the historical public support for reforms and dignity, earned through the sacrifices of youth, cannot be erased by the malicious propaganda of the ousted regime's supporters.

#Bangladesh #ProfYunus #NewYork #JFKAirport #HumanRights #News

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV

headline: 30 hours: CUET VC freed from confinement by DC and SP
summary: Prof Sk Shariful Alam was trapped in the administrative building for nearly 30 hours after students locked the gates during protests.
details: CUET Vice-Chancellor Prof Sk Shariful Alam was rescued from the campus on Tuesday evening after being confined for nearly 30 hours. Chattogram Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Zahidul Islam Mia and Superintendent of Police Masud Alam led the operation to escort him out.
caption:
Trapped for nearly 30 hours without water or electricity, the CUET Vice-Chancellor has finally been freed.

CUET Vice-Chancellor Prof Sk Shariful Alam was rescued from the campus on Tuesday evening after being confined for nearly 30 hours. Chattogram Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Zahidul Islam Mia and Superintendent of Police Masud Alam led the operation to escort him out.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo
